bull.b: Multiple products are showing strong prescription, unit, and revenue growth, reducing reliance on a single commercial asset. Continued adoption across dry eye, surgical, and ophthalmic treatment markets can support durable revenue expansion and improve operating leverage as the portfolio scales.

High gross margins indicate attractive product economics, while the shift to positive operating and free cash flow improves internal funding capacity. If sustained, this combination can support commercial investment, liquidity, and gradual balance-sheet repair despite current earnings pressure.

TYRVAYA broadens Harrow’s dry eye offering with a drop-free therapy that complements VEVYE and adds commercial resources. The expanded portfolio may increase physician cross-selling opportunities and management forecasts more than $30 million of TYRVAYA sales in 2027.

bear.b: The debt-funded balance sheet leaves Harrow with less flexibility if operating performance weakens or integration costs rise. Higher leverage can absorb more cash through financing obligations, constrain investment choices, and make sustained positive cash generation important for future deleveraging.

Strong gross margins have not yet translated into consistent profitability, indicating that operating costs or other expenses remain substantial. Rising commercial investment and planned TYRVAYA integration SG&A could prolong earnings pressure and delay the conversion of revenue growth into durable shareholder returns.

Meeting guidance depends on an unusually large second-half acceleration across product growth, channel normalization, salesforce productivity, and TYRVAYA integration. Any delay in these initiatives could leave revenue and profitability below targets, increasing pressure on cash resources and execution credibility.
